items.title: Banks offer semi-fixed loans to deploy surplus liquidity

items.title: SpiceJet to add 20 leased aircraft
items.summary: SpiceJet is leasing twenty aircraft to boost its flying capacity for the upcoming winter travel season.  These leased planes, a mix of Boeing and Airbus models, will arrive by mid-November.  The airline aims to operate around two hundred daily flights during this busy period.  This expansion will also support peak travel demand expected next year.  The leased aircraft offer a quicker way to increase capacity without outright purchases.

items.title: Drug cos refuse to take sole responsibility for overpricing
items.summary: Indian drugmakers oppose a proposal making them solely liable for medicine overpricing.  This regulatory move exempts retail chemists, hospitals, and nursing homes from penalties.  Pharmaceutical groups argue this unfairly burdens manufacturers already following pricing rules.  Retail chemists, however, welcome the safeguards for their members.  Manufacturers believe accountability should extend to those setting the final patient price.

items.title: LCR reset creates ₹2.1 Lakh-crore lending headroom for PSU Banks
items.summary: Public sector banks gained significant lending headroom after liquidity requirement relaxation. This allows them to sustain credit growth while deposit mobilisation remains relatively weak. Excess investment buffers could support incremental loan growth on their substantial loan books. Banks can now free up funds tied up in government bonds for lending. This improvement is visible at some of the largest state-owned lenders.

items.title: Stars display their ‘non-fiction’ side as streamers turn celebrity personas into show IPs
items.summary: The Indian entertainment industry is witnessing a surge in celebrities curating non-fiction series that revolve around their public identities. items.title: FSSAI to tighten scrutiny, weighs central ban on non-dairy paneer

items.title: India steps up coal supplies to power plants amid rising demand and falling stocks

Coal companies are being prompted to enhance their loading efficiency, while ongoing meetings will streamline coal production and logistics to maintain an uninterrupted supply flow to the power sector.
